summary:
Our project is an AI-powered interactive research and analytics platform designed to improve fire safety for future human space exploration. It brings together NASA's microgravity combustion experiments, including Saffire, FLEX, BASS and other related investigations, into one organised and accessible platform.

The system uses research documents and NASA references to build a structured research library. With a Python and FastAPI backend, it processes experiment information, extracts important findings and helps users explore and compare research. Interactive visualisations make available experimental measurements easier to understand, while an AI-powered research assistant helps users ask questions and discover insights from the collected documents.

By simplifying access to complex scientific research, our platform aims to identify important patterns in microgravity fire behaviour, support better understanding of combustion risks and contribute to safer spacecraft design and fire-safety planning for future Moon and Mars missions.
details:
Our project is an AI-powered research and analytics platform designed to improve understanding of fire behaviour in microgravity and support fire safety in future space missions.

The platform brings together NASA's combustion experiments, including SAFFIRE, FLEX, BASS and other related investigations, into one organised research library. Users can explore experiments, access research summaries and references, compare findings, and understand important scientific information through interactive visualisations. An AI-powered research assistant will help users ask questions and discover relevant insights from the collected research documents.

The system uses NASA research references and experiment summaries organised into JSON files. A Python and FastAPI backend processes this information and makes it accessible to the website. Our development tools include HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, FastAPI, JSON and an LLM API for AI-powered assistance.

The creative aspect of our project is bringing scattered and complex scientific research into a single interactive platform, making it easier for students, researchers and space enthusiasts to explore and understand microgravity combustion.

Our intended impact is to support better understanding of flame behaviour, smoke generation and combustion risks in reduced gravity, helping contribute to safer spacecraft environments and future human exploration of the Moon and Mars.

While developing the project, we considered scientific accuracy, reliable NASA references, accessibility of information, clarity of visualisations and the importance of distinguishing research-based findings from AI-generated interpretations.
